rules.statement: Use collection expressions instead of array and collection initializers, casting where generic inference needs it (e.g. `(byte[])[1, 2, 3]`).
rules.why: Template code style standard.
rules.check: Look for `new[] {...}`, `new List<T> {...}`, `Array.Empty<T>()` where a collection expression fits.

rules.statement: Declare local literal values with `const`, not `var`.
rules.why: Template convention for literals.
rules.check: Look for `var x = "literal";` or `var n = 5;` locals that are never reassigned.

rules.statement: Use `u8` string literals for bytes holding valid UTF-8 text, and explicit byte arrays only for invalid UTF-8 or error-condition cases.
rules.why: `u8` literals are clearer and avoid runtime encoding.
rules.check: Look for `Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes("literal")` or hand-written byte arrays of valid text.

rules.statement: Expose a fixed byte label used on every call as a `static ReadOnlySpan<byte> Label => "..."u8;` property, never a `const string` encoded on each call.
rules.why: Encoding a constant string per call allocates and wastes work.
rules.check: Look for a `const string` passed through `Encoding.*.GetBytes` in a hot path.

rules.statement: Put a trailing comma on every multi-line initializer, collection or enum member list.
rules.why: Template layout convention; keeps diffs minimal.
rules.check: Look for multi-line initializers or enums whose last item lacks a comma.

rules.statement: Put constants and static members at the top of a type, before instance members.
rules.why: Template layout convention.
rules.check: Look for `const` or `static` members declared after instance members.

rules.statement: Async methods return `ValueTask`/`ValueTask<T>`, end in `Async`, and take a `CancellationToken` as the last parameter; return `Task` only where a framework contract demands it (middleware `InvokeAsync`, minimal-API handler, an interface you don't own).
rules.why: Template async convention.
rules.check: Look for new async methods returning `Task`, missing the `Async` suffix, or lacking a trailing `CancellationToken`.

rules.statement: Await a `ValueTask` exactly once; call `.AsTask()` when it must be awaited twice or stored.
rules.why: A `ValueTask` may be backed by a pooled source that is invalid after one await.
rules.check: Look for a `ValueTask` stored in a field/variable and awaited more than once or awaited concurrently.

rules.statement: Never block on a task with `.Result`, `.Wait()`, `.GetAwaiter().GetResult()`, `Task.WaitAll` or `Task.WaitAny`; always `await`.
rules.why: Blocking causes deadlocks and thread starvation; these APIs are banned.
rules.check: Look for these calls in the diff.

rules.statement: Don't offload work to another thread unless it must leave the calling thread, and then use `Task.Run`, never `Task.Factory.StartNew` with an async delegate.
rules.why: `StartNew` with an async delegate returns `Task<Task>` whose inner exceptions are lost.
rules.check: Look for `Task.Factory.StartNew` or needless `Task.Run` wrapping.

rules.statement: Don't use `ConfigureAwait(false)` in code that runs only under ASP.NET Core or the generic host; in a library that UI or context-bound apps may consume, use `ConfigureAwait(false)` on every `await`.
rules.why: ASP.NET Core and the host install no `SynchronizationContext`, so it does nothing there, while context-bound consumers need it.
rules.check: Check whether the project is host-only or a general library and look for missing or superfluous `ConfigureAwait(false)`.

rules.statement: At an endpoint or middleware boundary, rethrow an `OperationCanceledException` caused by `HttpContext.RequestAborted`; never turn it into an error response, a retry or an audit write.
rules.why: It means the client went away.
rules.check: Look for catch blocks around request handling that swallow cancellation into a response, retry or audit.

rules.statement: A background loop treats an `OperationCanceledException` as a failure (logs and continues) unless its own stopping token is cancelled, e.g. `catch (Exception e) when (!stoppingToken.IsCancellationRequested)`.
rules.why: An `HttpClient` timeout throws `TaskCanceledException` with the stopping token untouched, and under `BackgroundServiceExceptionBehavior.StopHost` one escaped exception stops the process.
rules.check: Look for background loops that let `OperationCanceledException` escape or filter on exception type rather than on the stopping token.

rules.statement: Never use the null-forgiving operator `!`, even with a justification comment; restructure with `?? throw`, `[MemberNotNullWhen]`, an `is { } value` pattern or an early return (only test code may pass `null!` deliberately to the code under test).
rules.why: The compiler should prove non-nullness rather than be silenced.
rules.check: Look for postfix `!` on expressions in the diff outside `null!` arguments in tests.

rules.statement: Under a `where T : notnull` constraint, never use `field is null` on a `T?` field as the 'has a value' flag; track presence with a `bool` or constrain to `where T : struct`.
rules.why: For value types `T?` is plain `T`, so the null check is always false.
rules.check: Look for generic `T?` fields with `notnull` constraint tested against null.

rules.statement: Use `Debug.Assert` only for internal invariants, never for parsed or caller-supplied input; throw for anything derived from input.
rules.why: `Debug.Assert` is compiled out of Release builds, so bad input is accepted in production.
rules.check: Look for `Debug.Assert` on arguments, parsed values or external data.

rules.statement: Anchor a validating regular expression with `\z`, never `$`.
rules.why: In .NET `$` also matches before a trailing newline, so `^[a-z]+$` accepts `"acme\n"`.
rules.check: Look for validation regexes ending in `$`.

rules.statement: Carry an identifier that is compared byte for byte (a callback URL, an origin) as a `string` wherever it is stored, compared or sent, parsing a `Uri` only to inspect a part.
rules.why: `Uri` trims whitespace, drops empty query/fragment, ignores host case, and normalizes on `ToString()`/`AbsoluteUri`.
rules.check: Look for redirect URIs, origins or similar exact-match identifiers stored or compared as `Uri` or round-tripped through `Uri.ToString()`.

rules.statement: A value that is present but invalid fails closed: never treat a malformed field or header as absent, and reject a parameter or option the code doesn't honor yet instead of accepting and ignoring it.
rules.why: Silently ignoring malformed or unsupported input hides errors and weakens security.
rules.check: Look for parse failures falling back to the 'not provided' path, or accepted-but-ignored options.

rules.statement: Give a rule that guards data one implementation and call it from every path that accepts that data: startup configuration, API writes, imports, seeders and stored data on read.
rules.why: A check only startup runs lets a runtime write store what startup refuses.
rules.check: Look for validation added to only one entry path while other write paths skip it.

rules.statement: Prefer auto-properties to fields for state (static, instance and private), using a field only for a `ref`, `Interlocked`, `fixed` or `stackalloc` target; a `Lock` is a property (`private Lock Gate { get; } = new();`).
rules.why: Template convention for members.
rules.check: Look for new private fields that aren't `ref`/`Interlocked`/`fixed` targets.

rules.statement: Pick the narrowest property accessor: `{ get; }` for read-only state, `{ get; init; }` for immutable data, `{ get; set; }` only when mutation is needed, and an expression body for a simple computed property.
rules.why: Narrow accessors keep state immutable by default.
rules.check: Look for `set` accessors on properties that are never mutated after construction.

rules.statement: Use primary constructors wherever they can express the type, feeding parameters straight into get-only or `init` properties and putting `<param>` docs on the type; keep a classic constructor only for several public constructors, an initializer reading another instance member, or a body with branching, loops or `out`/`ref` work.
rules.why: Template convention for constructors.
rules.check: Look for classic constructors that only assign parameters to members.

rules.statement: Start every type and member at the narrowest visibility that works and widen to `public` only for a consumer contract, entry point or data consumers construct, never because a test needed it (tests use `InternalsVisibleTo`).
rules.why: An accidental `public` is a contract supported until the next major version.
rules.check: Look for new `public` types/members with no consumer reason, or made public for tests.

rules.statement: Keep a concrete implementation that consumers reach through DI `internal`; its interface is the public surface.
rules.why: Only the interface is the contract.
rules.check: Look for public default implementation classes registered in DI.

rules.statement: In a released library, treat any breaking public-surface change, or consumer-observable change in validation or security behavior, as requiring a major version; remove a member by marking it `[Obsolete]` in a minor version and deleting it in the next major.
rules.why: Consumers depend on both signatures and behavior.
rules.check: Look for removed/changed public members without `[Obsolete]` or version bump, or behavior changes in validation without a major bump (unless the project is pre-release).

rules.statement: In a released library, add new types, members or overloads instead of changing an existing public signature, including its nullability.
rules.why: Changing parameters, return type or nullability (`string` to `string?`) breaks callers.
rules.check: Look for altered parameter lists, return types or nullability annotations on public members.

rules.statement: Append members to a wire or `enum` vocabulary; never renumber or reorder existing members.
rules.why: Reordering changes the meaning of existing values.
rules.check: Look for enum diffs that insert, reorder or renumber members.

rules.statement: Never share one type between two packages that version independently; keep it in one owner or duplicate it on purpose.
rules.why: Shared types couple independent version lines.
rules.check: Look for linked source files or a type defined in one package and consumed as contract by an independently versioned one.

rules.statement: Every public-surface change to a library is recorded in `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt`, and that diff in the pull request must be intended.
rules.why: RS0016/RS0017 fail the build on unlisted or stale symbols; the reviewer confirms the change is deliberate.
rules.check: Check that the `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt` diff matches intended API changes.

rules.statement: In a pre-release project (before its first stable release), don't ask for `[Obsolete]` steps, compatibility overloads, major-version bumps or upcasters for public or stored-shape changes; changes happen in place.
rules.why: Compatibility rules don't bind before the first stable release (ADR-0015).
rules.check: Check the project's pre-release status (e.g. `pre-release: untracked` in AGENTS.md) before raising compatibility findings.

rules.statement: Make required inputs constructor parameters and optional inputs `init` properties; never add an optional value as a new constructor parameter, and model 'unspecified' as `null` resolved to a default inside the library.
rules.why: A new constructor parameter breaks binary compatibility once shipped.
rules.check: Look for new optional constructor parameters on public types.

rules.statement: Model a growing set of optional criteria as a `readonly record struct` with optional `init` properties instead of more positional parameters, keeping required identity keys positional.
rules.why: A new criterion is then a non-breaking addition.
rules.check: Look for methods gaining extra optional filter parameters.

rules.statement: Allow optional parameters on at most one overload of a method name; express an optional tail as explicit with- and without-argument overloads.
rules.why: Multiple overloads with optional parameters create ambiguity and fragile binding.
rules.check: Look for several overloads with default parameter values.

rules.statement: A configuration callback takes one growable options type (`Action<FooOptions>`), never extra parameters.
rules.why: A new setting is then a property, not a breaking signature change.
rules.check: Look for `Action<T1, T2>` or extra parameters on configuration methods.

rules.statement: Don't add behavior-selecting flag parameters; a `bool` or `enum` whose only job is to switch a method between two behaviors becomes two intention-revealing methods (a `bool` carried as data is fine).
rules.why: Flag parameters obscure intent at call sites.
rules.check: Look for `bool`/`enum` parameters that branch the whole method into two behaviors.

rules.statement: Use `InternalsVisibleTo` only for test projects and `DynamicProxyGenAssembly2`; production assemblies collaborate through public contracts.
rules.why: Production coupling through internals bypasses the contract.
rules.check: Look for `InternalsVisibleTo` naming a non-test assembly.

rules.statement: Keep an `*.Abstractions` assembly to contracts and data only: no method bodies with logic and no logging.
rules.why: Abstractions must stay a pure contract.
rules.check: Look for logic or logging added in an `.Abstractions` project.

rules.statement: Mark a type that is public only so the project's own assemblies can share it with `[EditorBrowsable(EditorBrowsableState.Never)]` and open its `<summary>` with "This API supports the {product} infrastructure and is not intended to be used directly from your code."
rules.why: It signals that the type isn't a supported consumer contract.
rules.check: Look for infrastructure-only public types missing the attribute or summary text.

rules.statement: When a replaceable public interface must apply a policy, put the policy behind its own public interface with an internal default.
rules.why: A replacement then resolves the policy instead of skipping it.
rules.check: Look for policy logic embedded only in a default implementation of a replaceable interface.

rules.statement: Make data, options, context, event and result types `sealed` with get-only or `init` members and concrete collections; use interfaces only for replaceable DI seams or read-only slices, not for data.
rules.why: Data types should be immutable and not extensible by accident.
rules.check: Look for unsealed data/options classes, settable members, or interfaces declared for data.

rules.statement: Seal a public leaf type, and never keep a public class unsealed or `public virtual` just so tests can mock it; mock its interface or make it `internal`.
rules.why: Sealing follows derivation intent, not testing convenience.
rules.check: Look for unsealed public classes or virtual members justified by mocking.

rules.statement: Prefer a `readonly record struct` for a small immutable value (an id, key, command or outcome); use a class for reference identity or a large or mutable payload.
rules.why: Template convention for value types.
rules.check: Look for small immutable values declared as classes.

rules.statement: Buffer by default: return a lazy `IEnumerable<T>` or `IAsyncEnumerable<T>` only for a large, unbounded, I/O-backed or usually short-circuited sequence, and never one that captures request state or that the caller enumerates twice or counts.
rules.why: Lazy sequences re-run work and can outlive the state they capture.
rules.check: Look for `yield return` or deferred LINQ returned from methods capturing request state or enumerated multiple times.

rules.statement: Copy every collection a type stores, injected `IEnumerable<T>` included, once into an owned collection chosen by use: `FrozenDictionary`/`FrozenSet` for repeated lookups, `ImmutableArray<T>` for iteration, `List<T>` only for a genuinely mutable working set.
rules.why: Storing a caller's collection lets it change underneath you or re-enumerate lazily.
rules.check: Look for constructors assigning a collection parameter directly to a member.

rules.statement: Use read-only interfaces (`IReadOnlyList<T>`, `IReadOnlyCollection<T>`, `IReadOnlySet<T>`) for parameters and computed return values, expose stored collection properties as their concrete immutable type, and prefer `params IEnumerable<T>` to `params T[]`.
rules.why: Signatures stay flexible while storage stays concrete and owned.
rules.check: Look for `List<T>`/`T[]` parameters, interface-typed stored properties, or `params T[]`.

rules.statement: Model an extensible set of named values as `public const string` names in a static class compared ordinally, with behavior in strategies resolved by name; reject unknown names, never `switch` over the names, encode inter-member relationships, or infer traits from a name.
rules.why: Consumers can add members without changing this code, and the strategy declares its own traits.
rules.check: Look for `switch` on such names, `EndsWith`-style trait inference, unknown names ignored, or an `enum` used for an open set.

rules.statement: Validate a registered set of named strategies when it is composed: an empty or duplicate name, or a reference to an unregistered member, throws an exception that names it.
rules.why: Misconfiguration should fail early and clearly.
rules.check: Look for strategy registries built without duplicate/empty/unknown-name checks.

rules.statement: Use an `enum` only for members fixed by something that can't grow without this code changing, and never mark a set that may grow `[Flags]`.
rules.why: Open sets belong in string names with strategies.
rules.check: Look for new enums or `[Flags]` enums over extensible concepts.

rules.statement: Persist or send an enum-like value as the member's name, never its ordinal.
rules.why: Ordinals break when members change.
rules.check: Look for casts of enums to int for storage or serialization, or missing string enum converters.

rules.statement: Keep secret material off the public surface: no secret in a `ToString()`, a public property of a loggable type, or an exception message.
rules.why: Those surfaces end up in logs and diagnostics.
rules.check: Look for secrets in `ToString` overrides, exception messages, or public properties of logged types.

rules.statement: Use `System.Text.Json`; Newtonsoft.Json is banned.
rules.why: Template standard serializer.
rules.check: Look for `Newtonsoft.Json` usings or references.

rules.statement: A DTO that reads, changes and writes back JSON it doesn't own keeps unknown members via `[JsonExtensionData] public Dictionary<string, JsonElement>? ExtensionData { get; set; }`.
rules.why: Otherwise unknown members are lost on round-trip.
rules.check: Look for round-tripped foreign JSON DTOs without extension data.

rules.statement: Serialize a payload stored at rest through one serializer that writes a versioned envelope `{ "$ver": N, "$payload": {...} }`, writes enums as strings, and refuses a non-envelope document with a descriptive `JsonException` (unless the project adopted the envelope over existing data).
rules.why: Versioning stored data allows safe evolution.
rules.check: Look for stored JSON written without the envelope or read without rejecting non-envelopes.

rules.statement: Once a stored payload shape has shipped in a stable release, evolve it additively: new members are optional (nullable or defaulted), never `required`, and a rename, removal or retype bumps the version with an upcaster.
rules.why: `System.Text.Json` enforces `required` on read, so every older row would fail.
rules.check: Look for `required` members or renamed/retyped members on stored DTOs without a version bump and upcaster.

rules.statement: Parse JSON into a `JsonElement` (`JsonElement.Parse` or `JsonSerializer.Deserialize<JsonElement>`), never `JsonDocument.Parse`.
rules.why: `JsonDocument.Parse` is banned (it needs disposal of pooled memory).
rules.check: Look for `JsonDocument.Parse`.

rules.statement: Check `ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Object` before reading members of JSON from the wire.
rules.why: `TryGetProperty` throws on non-object elements.
rules.check: Look for `TryGetProperty`/`GetProperty` on wire JSON without a prior `ValueKind` check.

rules.statement: Format and parse machine-facing values with `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture` and an exact `NumberStyles` (`Integer`, `Float`), never `NumberStyles.Any`, and parse a string as a date only where it is declared to be one.
rules.why: Culture-dependent or permissive parsing accepts wrong values; sniffing dates matches text like `"1.2"`.
rules.check: Look for `Parse`/`ToString` without invariant culture, `NumberStyles.Any`, or speculative `DateTime.TryParse`.

rules.statement: Match an opaque case-significant key (Base64Url id, hash, token) ordinally and verbatim; case-fold only values meant to match case-insensitively.
rules.why: Case-folding opaque keys causes false matches.
rules.check: Look for `OrdinalIgnoreCase`, `ToLower` or culture comparisons on ids, hashes or tokens.

rules.statement: A structured record emitted for others (an audit record, webhook or event payload) is documented in `docs/` and updated in the same change, carries a schema version bumped on each addition, omits absent members instead of writing `null`, and uses the same field names in logs, span tags and metric attributes.
rules.why: It is a contract consumers rely on.
rules.check: Look for payload changes without docs/version updates, null-writing, or inconsistent field names across telemetry.

rules.statement: Never let time arithmetic overflow: range-check before `DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds`, saturate when adding near `DateTimeOffset.MaxValue`, or compare elapsed time (`now - issuedAt > limit`).
rules.why: These operations throw on out-of-range input.
rules.check: Look for `FromUnixTimeSeconds` on untrusted input or `Add*` on possibly maximal timestamps.

rules.statement: Put one type per file, with an interface and its implementation in separate files (`IFoo` and `IFoo<T>` may share).
rules.why: Template organization rule.
rules.check: Look for files declaring multiple top-level types.

rules.statement: Name the single internal DI implementation of `IFoo` that consumers never name `DefaultFoo`, except variants named for what makes them specific, framework-interface implementations following framework naming, and public data types consumers construct.
rules.why: Template naming convention.
rules.check: Look for sole default implementations named otherwise (e.g. `FooImpl`, `FooService`).

rules.statement: Don't nest types, except a private type that must close over the enclosing type's generic parameter, or a nested static class of related `const` values.
rules.why: Template organization rule.
rules.check: Look for nested classes, records or enums outside those exceptions.

rules.statement: Organize folders by purpose, keep consumer entry points at the project root, and never create a catch-all folder or namespace such as `Helpers`, `Utils`, `Common`, `Misc` or `Logic`.
rules.why: Readers find code by purpose.
rules.check: Look for new catch-all folders/namespaces or folders mixing unrelated purposes.

rules.statement: A feature folder holds its contract, data types and default implementation and registers its own services through an `Add*Services()` extension.
rules.why: Features stay self-contained.
rules.check: Look for feature registrations scattered outside the feature.

rules.statement: Internal types use a namespace matching their folder, while a library's public types keep a shallow, stable namespace under the root that doesn't change when the file moves.
rules.why: Public namespaces are a contract.
rules.check: Look for public types whose namespace mirrors deep folders, or namespace changes on moved public types.

rules.statement: Name an interface for its role (`IPaymentHandler`, `IOrderStore`), adding a qualifier only when the bare noun collides with a well-known framework type.
rules.why: Template naming convention.
rules.check: Look for interface names that are vague or needlessly qualified.

rules.statement: Keep `Program.cs` to a flat list of `AddX`, `UseX` and `MapX` calls; move any `if`, loop, policy builder, `new`, constant or configuration read into an extension in the owning project, leaving only host-specific inputs (database provider and connection string, production secrets, Kestrel HTTPS defaults).
rules.why: Composition stays readable and features stay turnkey.
rules.check: Look for logic, literals or configuration reads added to `Program.cs`.

rules.statement: A library never calls `ConfigureHttpsDefaults`.
rules.why: Kestrel keeps only the last action, so it silently replaces or is replaced by the host's TLS settings.
rules.check: Look for `ConfigureHttpsDefaults` in library code.

rules.statement: Register a project's services from one registration class using `TryAdd*` so consumers can replace any default, keeping registration out of the types that do the work.
rules.why: A host replaces a default by registering its own first.
rules.check: Look for `Add*` instead of `TryAdd*`, or registration code inside working types.

rules.statement: Register a stateless capability as a singleton and a long-running loop as `AddHostedService<T>` over a `BackgroundService`.
rules.why: Template DI lifetime convention.
rules.check: Look for stateless services registered scoped/transient or loops not run as hosted services.

rules.statement: The project owning a feature registers its framework dependencies (routing, `IHttpClientFactory`, `TimeProvider`) with `TryAdd*` rather than relying on a host call pulling them in by accident.
rules.why: Composing the feature should be turnkey.
rules.check: Look for features consuming such services without registering them.

rules.statement: Choose the DI shape on purpose: a single service for a capability, `TryAddEnumerable` strategy collections for implementations iterated or selected, a mediator pipeline only for cross-cutting wrapping, and state any handler ordering explicitly, never via registration order.
rules.why: Registration order is an invisible, fragile dependency.
rules.check: Look for code relying on registration order or the wrong DI shape.

rules.statement: Give each built-in strategy registered with `TryAddEnumerable` its own class.
rules.why: `TryAddEnumerable` keeps one registration per implementation type, so a second instance of the same class is silently dropped.
rules.check: Look for multiple `TryAddEnumerable` registrations of instances of the same type.

rules.statement: Write extension members as C# 14 `extension(Receiver receiver) { ... }` blocks, with one receiver type per static class.
rules.why: Template convention; CA1708 enforces one receiver per class.
rules.check: Look for classic `this` extension methods or mixed receivers in one class.

rules.statement: When two unrelated receiver interfaces are both implemented by a common concrete type (e.g. `IDictionary<,>` and `IReadOnlyDictionary<,>`), write one extension on their common base and fast-path the specific types inside.
rules.why: An overload per interface makes calls on the concrete type ambiguous (CS0121).
rules.check: Look for parallel extension overloads on such interface pairs.

rules.statement: Guard an extension receiver against `null` with `nameof(receiver)`, suppressing CA2208 with a tight `#pragma warning disable/restore` and reason rather than dropping the name.
rules.why: Extension members can be called on null, and CA2208 doesn't recognize the receiver as a parameter.
rules.check: Look for extension members missing a receiver null check or omitting the param name.

rules.statement: Never cache per-request state on a singleton (e.g. `_result ??= await ...`); keep it on the request or a scoped service not captured by a singleton.
rules.why: The first request's answer leaks to every later one.
rules.check: Look for mutable members on singletons assigned from request data.

rules.statement: Implement an 'accept once' check (replay guard, idempotency key) as an atomic add-if-absent on a shared store and a shared count as an atomic increment, never a read followed by a write.
rules.why: Two concurrent requests both pass a get-then-set; `IDistributedCache` can't express it.
rules.check: Look for get-then-set patterns on replay or idempotency state, or `IDistributedCache` used for them.

rules.statement: Build shared-store keys from length-prefixed components, hashing caller-supplied parts to a fixed size, and scope them by purpose.
rules.why: Keys are then unambiguous, bounded, and partitions don't collide.
rules.check: Look for keys built by plain concatenation of caller input.

rules.statement: A library never registers a host-wide cache or store; the host chooses it.
rules.why: The host owns shared infrastructure.
rules.check: Look for library registration of `IDistributedCache` or similar host-wide stores.

rules.statement: Consume a single-use record (code, one-time link, invitation) with one atomic take after every check passes and before its effect, never a read followed by a remove.
rules.why: Read-then-remove races; taking after checks leaves a refused request's record usable.
rules.check: Look for get-then-delete of single-use records or takes before validation.

rules.statement: Update a shared record with compare-and-swap on the version read, via a read-modify-write update function the store reapplies after a lost race; never write a value computed from an earlier read, and retry (not `412`) operations whose outcome doesn't depend on what was read.
rules.why: Prevents lost updates under concurrency.
rules.check: Look for blind overwrites of stored records or update logic outside a retrying update function.

rules.statement: When a request and a background pass can both act on one record, run the effect only in the caller whose write claimed it, on the record as claimed.
rules.why: Acting on an earlier read duplicates or corrupts effects.
rules.check: Look for effects triggered from a read without a claiming write.

rules.statement: Have a store report a lost optimistic-concurrency race with its own exception type, never an ORM type, and handle it in one place.
rules.why: Callers shouldn't depend on the ORM.
rules.check: Look for `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` leaking past the store or handled in many handlers.

rules.statement: Make writes that a background loop retries idempotent by recording an identity in the same unit of work and skipping writes whose identity already exists.
rules.why: A save can commit and still fail at its caller.
rules.check: Look for retried background writes without an idempotency identity.

rules.statement: Run an effect that must follow a committed change with `CancellationToken.None` bounded by its own timeout, keeping the request's token for steps before the commit.
rules.why: A client disconnect could otherwise leave the change committed without its effect.
rules.check: Look for post-commit effects using the request's cancellation token.

rules.statement: Send an effect that must survive a crash right after commit (message, webhook, notification) through an outbox written in the same transaction and delivered at least once by a background worker with back-off, with an idempotent handler.
rules.why: Direct sends after commit can be lost.
rules.check: Look for direct post-commit sends of must-happen effects.

rules.statement: A receiver of retried deliveries records the dedupe key only after handling succeeds and on failure answers so the sender retries.
rules.why: A failed attempt must never be refused later as a replay.
rules.check: Look for dedupe keys stored before handling completes.

rules.statement: Never let correctness depend on process-local state when multiple instances can run: durable or cross-instance state goes to a database or shared store, in-memory caches hold only rebuildable data, and nothing durable is written to the local file system.
rules.why: Instances don't share memory or disk.
rules.check: Look for static/singleton fields or local files holding authoritative state.

rules.statement: Give a per-instance cache entry an absolute lifetime and announce changes after commit as a best-effort, id-only hint whose failure is logged without failing the write; drop possibly invalidated entries after a reconnect.
rules.why: Bounds staleness without coupling writes to messaging.
rules.check: Look for sliding-only cache entries, data in invalidation messages, or writes failing on announcement errors.

rules.statement: Converge derived state by an idempotent reconciliation pass that compares current input with durably stored last-reconciled state, run by one instance under an expiring lease, never by replaying events or draining an in-memory queue.
rules.why: Reconciliation is safe to rerun after a restart.
rules.check: Look for derived state maintained by in-memory queues or event replay.

rules.statement: Never run work proportional to data size (a pass over every record) inside a request; run it in the background.
rules.why: It makes request latency unbounded.
rules.check: Look for full-table scans or loops over all entities in request handlers.

rules.statement: Hand work to the background as a snapshot (ids, actor, trace context), never `HttpContext` or a request-scoped service; run each item in its own `CreateAsyncScope()` under the app's stopping token, log per-item failures and continue, and queue in a bounded `Channel<T>` with a fixed number of consumers.
rules.why: Request objects die with the request and unbounded queues exhaust memory.
rules.check: Look for captured `HttpContext`/scoped services in background work, unbounded channels, or one failure stopping the batch.

rules.statement: A hosted service whose `StopAsync` does work runs it once and never throws: memoize the stop task under a `Lock`, serialize it with periodic work, and log what it couldn't finish.
rules.why: A host can be stopped twice at once and dispose the provider under the other stop.
rules.check: Look for `StopAsync` implementations that can run twice or throw.

rules.statement: Give a table that grows with use a configured retention, pruned by a periodic hosted service in bounded batches (each its own unit of work, repeating while full) over an indexed filter column.
rules.why: Unbounded growth degrades the store.
rules.check: Look for new growing tables without retention, unbounded deletes, or unindexed prune filters.

rules.statement: Don't expose a public API that disables a security control or weakens it below its safe baseline; settings may only supply values or swap in an equal or stronger control.
rules.why: Correct by default.
rules.check: Look for options like `DisableValidation`, `AllowInsecure` or similar.

rules.statement: When only some endpoints accept a kind of caller, refuse it everywhere by default and let permitted endpoints opt in through endpoint metadata.
rules.why: A per-endpoint deny check is missing from the next endpoint added.
rules.check: Look for deny checks added per endpoint rather than default-deny with opt-in metadata.

rules.statement: Treat an unset or empty allow-list at a trust boundary (algorithms, origins, schemes, callers) as permitting nothing, never as 'allow all'.
rules.why: A missing list must not open the boundary.
rules.check: Look for `if (list.Count == 0) return true` style checks.

rules.statement: Make a correctness guard (replay check, authorization, lockout) fail closed when its store is unreachable, a capacity guard (rate limiter, cache) fail open behind a short timeout with once-per-outage logging and a metric, and answer a store outage with `503`, never `401`, `404` or 'not found'.
rules.why: Outages must neither bypass security nor sign users out or read as missing data.
rules.check: Look for store exceptions mapped to allow, `401` or `404`.

rules.statement: Decode untrusted bytes as text with a throwing encoding (`new UTF8Encoding(false, throwOnInvalidBytes: true)`), not `Encoding.UTF8`.
rules.why: `Encoding.UTF8` silently substitutes replacement characters.
rules.check: Look for `Encoding.UTF8.GetString` on untrusted input.

rules.statement: Never let a secret (password, token, key, connection string, request credential) reach a log entry, audit event, stored request copy or served OpenAPI document/UI; record ids and metadata instead, pre-filling dev credentials only in Development.
rules.why: These surfaces are widely readable.
rules.check: Look for secrets passed to loggers, audit events, stored requests or OpenAPI examples.

rules.statement: Compare a secret, MAC, hash or verifier with `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals`, never `==`, `string.Equals` or `SequenceEqual`.
rules.why: Non-constant-time comparisons leak timing information.
rules.check: Look for equality operators on secret material.

rules.statement: Generate application-issued credentials (API keys, client secrets) on the server, show them once at creation, store only a salted hash or protected value, never return them from reads, lists or logs, and rotate by creating the new one before deleting the old.
rules.why: Limits exposure of credentials.
rules.check: Look for client-supplied secrets, plaintext storage, or secrets returned by read endpoints.

rules.statement: Give every outbound call its own timeout, bounded jittered retries (`Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience`), and read response bodies under a size limit.
rules.why: Remote calls must not hang or exhaust memory.
rules.check: Look for `HttpClient` calls without timeout/resilience or unbounded `ReadAsStringAsync`.

rules.statement: Fetch user-supplied or user-registered URLs only through one named `HttpClient` whose `ConnectCallback` refuses loopback, private and link-local addresses and connects to the vetted address, requires `https`, sets `AllowAutoRedirect = false`, and enforces its byte limit while streaming, with no setting to disable the check.
rules.why: Prevents SSRF and DNS rebinding; `Content-Length` is only a hint.
rules.check: Look for user-supplied URLs fetched with a general client or redirects enabled.

rules.statement: Fetch a shared remote resource (metadata document, key set) once via a `ConcurrentDictionary<TKey, Lazy<Task<T>>>` entry that removes itself, bounded by its own timeout rather than a caller's token (callers use `WaitAsync`), and cache failures for a configured time.
rules.why: An unreachable source shouldn't cost every request a timeout or be cancelled by one caller.
rules.check: Look for per-request fetches of shared resources or fetches tied to a caller's token.
